Live Copilot sessions

Live Copilot CLI sessions per Codex thread (the default): why they exist, how requests continue, reseed or fall back, and what stays on disk.

About 20 min read · 11 sections

On this page
01 Messages interleaved with pending results 02 Caller tool identity 03 What a session is made of 04 How a request is served 05 Admission 06 Waiting for tools 07 Stopping a session 08 Safety 09 Billing and diagnostics 10 Restarts and upgrades 11 Limits

The gateway keeps one copilot --headless process and one session per Codex thread, the way the Copilot CLI runs on its own. The session holds the native history, the caller's tool calls wait inside it as pending external tool requests, and each gateway request sends only what is new. This is the default (copilotSessions.mode: "live").

Why: a new session on every request ("oneshot") reads only the fixed system message and tool list from Copilot's prompt cache and writes the rest of the history to the cache again. In a three-round tool loop on gpt-6-luna with a 3.7k-token prompt, rounds 2 and 3 each read 1.6k tokens from the cache, wrote 2.2k to 2.3k and cost about 30 million nano-AIU. In one session, every follow-up call reads the whole earlier prompt from the cache and writes only the new tail. With a 12k-token prompt, the first call wrote 12k tokens and cost 151 million nano-AIU, and each follow-up call cost about 13 million. In the live check on CLI 1.0.97, gateway rounds 2 and 3 of the 3.7k-token loop read 98% of their input from the cache, wrote under 60 tokens and cost 4.8 to 6.0 million nano-AIU. Observed gateway traffic before live sessions cost about 9.5 times what the same work costs natively.

{ "id": "copilot", "type": "copilot-subscription", "copilotSessions": { "mode": "live", "max": 4, "parkMinutes": 30, "toolWaitMinutes": 25 } }

Every field is optional, and a provider with no copilotSessions at all runs live with the defaults below. The daemon reads a change on its next request. "oneshot" (or "replay", accepted as another name) turns live sessions off: running turns finish, and the provider's parked sessions close on its next request, or at once when the daemon reloads the configuration (mode_oneshot). A reload also closes the sessions of a Copilot provider that was removed or whose id or authDirectory changed (provider_removed): no request would ever reach it again, and the session folders hold the conversation log. A session whose turn is running closes when the turn ends, and so does one that was still starting when its provider was removed (it closes when the request that started it ends). A gateway generation that an in-place upgrade starts does the same for the sessions it adopts from the release before it: those whose provider its configuration no longer serves close at once. An ordinary live request that cannot continue receives a final refusal instead of silently switching to one-shot. See provider reuse.

Setting Default Meaning
mode live live keeps a session per thread; oneshot or replay starts a session per request
max 4 Live sessions in the whole process (1–16). A session being started counts toward it
parkMinutes 30 Idle time before a session closes (5–240). Copilot's prompt cache lasted 30 minutes for gpt-6-luna and 5 minutes for claude-haiku-5.5 in the measurements; a session parked longer still continues, at about the price of a reseed, and keeps its native history
toolWaitMinutes 25 How long a session waits for Codex to run a tool before it closes (1–25). The wait is the smaller of this and parkMinutes: with parkMinutes: 10 a session waiting for tools closes after 10 minutes

Messages interleaved with pending results

Developer/user messages and agent reports may arrive before, between or after pending tool results. The gateway continues the same live session only when the history contains every pending result exactly once and all new caller messages are fully accounted for. It acknowledges those messages as steering, then releases the results once. Original roles, item numbers and image ownership stay associated with their messages; tool results never render as caller text. Missing/duplicate results, new tool calls, edited history and other mismatches retain the preserved-session refusal. No full-history replay or compaction is introduced by this recovery.

Caller tool identity

Copilot may return a caller-visible alias instead of the generated native tool name. The gateway accepts exact, unambiguous spellings from the current caller catalog, using the shared Claude identity bindings. Arguments, call IDs and the original caller namespace remain unchanged. Unknown, removed and ambiguous names still fail before dispatch; no prefix stripping or fuzzy matching is used. A copilot_tool_rejected record with nameClass: declared_alias from an older release identifies this former mapping refusal rather than an invented tool.

What a session is made of

One-shot requests and live sessions are built the same way, so a fallback never changes what the model sees.

  • System message: the gateway's guidance, the tool-name mapping, and the caller's leading system and developer messages. It is fixed for the session's life.
  • History: one user message per conversation item, oldest first, each between <<item N role>> and <</item>> lines. A seed sends all items with session.sendMessages; a continuation sends only the new ones. Replayed calls to a currently declared tool use its same native name as the tool declaration. Arguments, custom input, call IDs and results stay unchanged, and the live ledger keeps the caller's original identities. Ambiguous or unavailable old tool names remain historical names; replay never makes them available.
  • Images: a history item's images are written (mode 0600) to the images folder of the CLI's private folder and attached to the item's message as file attachments; the message text names each one. Their bytes never travel inside a message, because one RPC message to the CLI is limited to 16 MiB and a few screenshots pass that. The files go with the folder. A request that is cancelled (or whose session ends) while its images are being written writes no further image: the check comes before each one, the write in flight ends before the folder is removed, and an images folder is never created in a CLI folder that is already gone. A tool output's images can only travel inline, as binary results of the waiting call, so a tool result whose JSON exceeds 12 MiB is not handed over: the thread reseeds (large_tool_result), and the seed sends those images as files.
  • Tools: the caller's whole catalog, always, whatever the tool choice. Each tool is an external tool the caller answers, named tool_<name>_<hash> after its identity, so reordering the catalog changes nothing. The list is sorted. skipPermission is on, every tool is defer: "never", and toolSearch and largeOutput are off: the CLI never hides a caller tool behind its own tool search, never saves a large result to a file, and never runs a tool itself.
  • Tool choice: a forced or required choice, or none, is a line on the last message (Use the required caller tool …, Use one of the caller tools., Do not call any caller tool; answer directly.). A model that ignores it fails the request.

How a request is served

Copilot's SDK protocol defines an omitted assistant.message.toolRequests[].type as function. The gateway accepts that documented default while retaining exact catalog-name matching, distinct call IDs, object argument checks and client-owned execution. Explicit non-function types remain rejected because the gateway declares only external functions. Treating a missing type as malformed previously failed valid tool calls and made Codex retry their response streams. This matches the official SDK event contract for CLI 1.0.97. arguments is likewise optional there: a call that omits it is forwarded with no arguments, while an explicit non-object payload (including custom tools missing their string input) remains rejected.

  • Spawn: the thread has no session. A new process starts and the history is sent once. Telemetry reports spawned.
  • Continue: the request carries the history the session already has plus new items. Public reasoning summaries retain their reasoning type and rendered positions. They do not become extra assistant answers in the live ledger, so summaries replayed alongside tool calls do not block the pending results. Opaque reasoning from another transport is never passed to the CLI. New user items are sent as user messages. Tool outputs are handed to the session's pending external tool requests with session.tools.handlePendingToolCall, each to the request of the call it answers, whatever order the outputs arrive in, at most 16 at a time (the CLI connection takes 32 requests in flight). An empty output is handed over as (no output), so the waiting call is still answered. The prefix is read from the cache, the follow-up model calls are agent-initiated, and the request is billed for its own model calls only. An effort change between turns keeps the session: the gateway calls session.model.switchTo, which keeps the cache.
  • Queued caller updates: complete pending results followed by user/developer messages continue the same session. Each new item is acknowledged through immediate session.send before any result is delivered. Old adopted instances without that capability preserve and refuse rather than dropping messages.
  • Controlled reseed: genuine model/system/tool or window changes, oversized inline results, an idle/dead/expired session found before placement, or a completed native Messages caller-owned history replacement can require a new process. A failed session during the current placement cannot seed again in that request.
  • Preserve and refuse: unexplained prefix_diverged, unexpected_tail, forced_choice, effort_midturn, an explicit effort_rejected, or tool_request_missing leaves a usable session and its pending tools intact. Matching corrected input can continue it. An uncertain effort change closes the unsafe session and returns a final continuity refusal.
  • Standalone: explicit compaction/prewarm/memory requests and anonymous first questions can use one-shot. Historical anonymous conversations require an ID.
  • Final continuity refusal: concurrency, capacity, startup, tool-delivery, stream and attachment failures cannot silently replay history. This also applies after partial output/usage. Images and forced choices remain supported on compatible live paths.

Admission

While every slot holds a session, a new thread first waits for a session that is already closing, then can take a session idle at least 30 minutes. Warm and running sessions, and sessions whose own request is being placed, are never evicted. Without a cold slot, the newcomer receives a final capacity refusal. An evicted session's process and folder are gone before its replacement starts. The evicted thread reseeds on its next request (evicted). If that request arrives while the old session is still ending, it takes over the slot: the old session stops counting toward max and the request waits until its process and folder are gone before it starts its new session. Sessions being started count toward max, in arrival order, so concurrent starts never hold more sessions than the cap. Any session that is still closing when its thread's next request comes no longer holds the thread or a slot in the same way; the request waits until it is gone and starts a new session, reporting how the old one ended (for example tool_wait_expired).

Waiting for tools

Copilot fails a pending external tool request 1,800 seconds after it was issued, and the runtime then makes a model call of its own, which is billed. The gateway closes a session that is waiting for tool outputs after toolWaitMinutes (25 at most) or parkMinutes, whichever is smaller, before that happens: session.abort, then SIGKILL. The next request reseeds (tool_wait_expired).

Between requests the gateway accepts only housekeeping: the pending calls' own tool.execution_start and external_tool.requested events, session.info, session.warning, session.title_changed, pending_messages.modified, session.usage_info, session.usage_checkpoint, session.idle (CLI 1.0.97 sends it right after assistant.idle), and known model-completion metadata. Model-call and model-turn start aliases, including model.model_call_started, remain refused. It also accepts the CLI's start-up announcements session.start and session.managed_settings_resolved until the session's first request, and a session.model_change that confirms the effort change the gateway asked for (the CLI sends it before it answers session.model.switchTo; the gateway recognizes it even when it is read after the next request attached). A confirmation for another effort than the one asked for ends the session (effort_mismatch), and the request is refused. Anything else kills the session at once, before it can spend: a tool.execution_complete or external_tool.completed for a call nobody answered (the timeout, or a failed call), a model call, any assistant output or usage, compaction, truncation or an error, a model change nobody asked for, a permission request, a sub-agent event, or a tool request for a call that is not pending. A session that misbehaves while it is starting is never handed to a request; the request receives a final refusal (spawn_failed). A timer cannot be trusted alone, because a sleeping Mac stops it while the CLI's clock goes on.

Hot adoption replaces only the existing session's event router with the current v1-compatible policy. Its process, pump, history, timers and pending tools remain intact. Registry adoption and request placement both apply the router, so warm sessions receive the updated housekeeping and model-start guards too.

Stopping a session

Cancelling a request, a reseed, an eviction, a tool-wait expiry and any violation end the session the same way: session.abort (bounded to 2 seconds, errors ignored), then SIGKILL of the CLI's whole process group, which is its own group, and the removal of its folder. A parked session that is not running anything needs no abort and is killed the same way. A one-shot request is closed the same way whenever its CLI may hold an unanswered tool request: a turn that ended in tool calls, a tool request the gateway rejected (a disabled or other tool than the required one, a native tool), any failure, a cancellation once its session exists, and a client that stops reading. Only a one-shot turn that ended idle with a complete text answer, and so nothing pending, is deleted (session.delete) and stopped with SIGTERM; once a session exists no other end ever sends either, because a runtime that is told to exit can fail a pending call and make a model call of its own. A connection that fails (an event backlog, an invalid frame) ends its CLI with SIGKILL. Only a CLI whose request is cancelled or fails while the connection is still being opened (before the handshake ends) has no session and nothing pending, and is stopped with SIGTERM. A request cancelled while its CLI is still ending sends nothing more: the prompt of a one-shot request, and the messages or tool results of a live one, are not sent after the cancellation, because each would start a model call nobody waits for. A cancelled request stops reading the model at once but ends only when its session is gone (about 2 seconds: the abort is bounded to 2 seconds, then the CLI is killed and its folder removed), handing over the usage the CLI reports meanwhile. A process outside the CLI's group that keeps the CLI's output open (a helper the CLI detached) does not hold the request: once the CLI has exited and its output has been silent for half a second, or at most about 5 seconds (100 ticks) after the exit when output keeps arriving, the gateway closes its pipes and the request ends. A reseed or an eviction waits for the old session to be gone. Closing a session under a running request fails that request at once with a final continuity refusal (stream_failed). The next independent request after a cancellation reseeds, because the half-written answer cannot be matched against what Codex replays. A request that has already finished is not affected when the client closes the connection afterwards.

A complete answer whose assistant.idle event does not follow within 5 seconds still ends the request normally; the session then closes (idle_missing).

Safety

  • The CLI sees only the gateway's tools. A permission request, a tool start or request for any other name, a sub-agent event, BYOK usage, another model or output with no request attached kills the session and fails the request. The gateway still answers no host request, and the CLI is spawned with --no-auto-update, --disable-builtin-mcps, --no-custom-instructions and --no-remote-export, and the session store off. Copilot 1.0.103 retired --no-remote (the CLI exits when it is given) and made remote hosting opt-in through explicit --host-* flags, which the gateway never passes. The gateway therefore adds --no-remote only for a verified managed installation older than 1.0.103, and for a CLI from PATH, whose version it does not know: an old one stays without incoming remote control, and a new one refuses to start rather than start without that guarantee. Provider maintenance probes the same command line.
  • The session store stays off, so no session rows or session folders are added to ~/.copilot, and the CLI's configuration folder is private. The CLI does write a log of the conversation, including prompts and tool results, to session-state/<id>/events.jsonl in that folder. In one-shot mode it lives for seconds; in live mode it lives as long as the session. The folder is $TMPDIR/harness-gateway-copilot-<uid>/gateway-copilot-live-<owner pid>-<owner start>-<random> (one-shot: gateway-copilot-run-…), with the gateway's pid and start time in base 36 (the start time is left out when ps cannot read it), mode 0700. The parent harness-gateway-copilot-<uid> is the gateway's own folder in the OS temp folder, mode 0700 and owned by you; a symlink or another user's folder in its place is refused. The folder holds the CLI's own TMPDIR and the history's images, for every CLI the gateway starts. It is removed when the session closes, parks out, is evicted, crashes, is cancelled or is retired, and by every gateway shutdown hook. If the gateway exits through process.exit or the end of its event loop without closing them, an exit handler kills every Copilot CLI it started (live, one-shot, starting or closing) and removes their folders synchronously; a folder that could not be removed when its CLI closed (the removal is retried five times) stays on that list for the handler, and closing never fails the request or the gateway because of it. If the gateway is killed outright, its CLIs exit when their input closes (measured on CLI 1.0.97), and the next gateway removes every folder whose owner no longer runs when it starts, before its first request and whatever any provider's mode is. Each sweep reads the parent folder; it does not read the whole OS temp folder, which can hold hundreds of thousands of entries, except once and then again after a week, for the folders of older releases (below). An owner no longer runs when its pid is dead or now belongs to a process with another start time (ps -o lstart), so a reused pid keeps nothing; folders that another user owns are never removed, and a parent that is not a real folder you own is neither read nor trusted. Folders that older releases left straight in the OS temp folder without an owner (gateway-copilot-<random>) are removed once they are more than two hours old, longer than any request runs; that weekly read of the OS temp folder is recorded by the .legacy-scan file in the parent.
  • No caller prompt, tool argument or output goes to gateway logs, telemetry or the usage ledger.

Billing and diagnostics

The app's Diagnostics screen and gateway diagnostics now summarize Copilot session outcomes, rebuild reasons and cache coverage. New session events include provider and model identity. Tool-call failures carry fixed structural reasons, so an unknown tool, duplicate call ID, malformed call and invalid argument shape are distinguishable without storing tool arguments. Historical generic failures retain their original level of detail. See diagnostics.

The usage ledger records one row per gateway request with that request's own cache read, cache write, reasoning and nano-AIU totals, so the saving shows directly in the cache-read share of inputTokens and in nanoAiu per request; see diagnostics. Usage that the CLI reported before a request failed or was cancelled is still counted, live or one-shot: the request reports it as one running total of every model call it made, and the interrupted or failed copilot_session event already includes it. When a request stops early (the caller left, it was cancelled or timed out, or the gateway is shutting down), the server keeps reading the provider for up to 3 seconds, for usage only, even if it was waiting for a slow client to take earlier output. At shutdown it waits for those requests to write their ledger rows before its final flush, but the process leaves 1.5 seconds after the drain deadline at the latest. Before it leaves, it writes a failed ledger row and a request_failed record for every request still running, with the usage its provider had reported so far, and then flushes telemetry and the ledger, so a request stopped at shutdown never loses what it had already cost. Usage that arrives after the process has left is not recorded. A cancelled request hands its total over as the CLI reports it, live or one-shot: each usage the CLI reports while it is being aborted (session.abort is bounded to 2 seconds before SIGKILL) is added to the request's totals and handed over at once as the running total, without waiting for the CLI to be killed, so a process that leaves in between has the usage already. A live request ends once its session is gone; the interrupted event is written then, so it counts that usage too.

copilot_session telemetry has one event per decision or end:

Field Values
outcome spawned, continued, reseeded, fallback, interrupted (the request was cancelled), reaped (parked or tool-wait timer), evicted, crashed, closed (ended on purpose)
missReason on reseeded and fallback: the reasons above. On an end (closed, reaped, evicted, crashed): why it ended — a reseed reason, interrupted, idle_missing, tool_wait_expired, mode_oneshot (the provider switched to one-shot), provider_removed (a reload removed the provider or changed its id or auth directory), shutdown, stopped, or for crashed: foreign_tool, permission, sub_agent, unannounced_tool, unattended_output, unattended_completion, backlog, exited, delivery_rejected (a tool result was not confirmed), or the code of the error that failed the request
threadKey the first 8 hex of the thread's session key
liveSessions live sessions after the event
divergedAt on prefix_diverged and unexpected_tail: the index of the first item that did not match
parkedMs how long the session had been idle when the request or end came
failed on a request that failed after reaching a session
initiator, inputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, outputTokens, reasoningTokens, nanoAiu, toolCalls the request's own totals; initiator is user (a new message started the first call), agent (the session's own follow-up) or mixed

A session that never served a request (it failed while starting) has no end event; its request's fallback event says why. request_completed and request_failed carry the same initiator, cacheWriteTokens, reasoningTokens and nanoAiu for every Copilot request.

copilot_session_violation records the fixed event type, reason, state and pending call count before an unsolicited event closes a session. Warning/title text, tool arguments and event bodies are excluded. Unknown event names are recorded as unknown; documented title, warning and queue-change notifications are metadata, so they do not destroy a warm session.

Restarts and upgrades

Upgrading from a release that replayed caller tool names rebuilds each live session once because the system message's tool-name guidance changed.

An in-place upgrade keeps the sessions: the registry lives on the versioned global symbol harness-gateway/copilot-sessions/v1, so the new runtime adopts the one it finds, with its sessions, and the next request of a thread continues the running process unless something the session was created with changed. A registry with another interface version is replaced, not adopted; its sessions still close on their own timers or at shutdown. Sessions adopted from before typed reasoning support can match their exact former summary-to-assistant prefix. A bounded compatibility check accepts only a complete digest match before applying the ordinary pending-tool and settings checks. It never edits a refused session or resends its history. New sessions use only the typed ledger; an accepted continuation commits that format for an adopted one. The gateway counts as busy, so an idle restart or a self-update waits, while a session is starting or generating, or has waited for tool outputs for less than 10 minutes; a longer wait gains nothing from its cache. On shutdown, after the request drain, every session is closed: a turn that runs or waits for tools is aborted, then the process group is killed and the folder removed.

Limits

A request that arrives with a tool output the session cannot match reseeds instead of guessing. The protocol details come from measurements on Copilot CLI 1.0.97, and session.sendMessages, session.tools.handlePendingToolCall, session.abort and session.model.switchTo are experimental there; run a short live check against the installed CLI after upgrading it. The last check (October 2026) covered a three-round tool loop, an effort change between turns, Stop while a tool waited, a request without a thread id, shutdown with a parked session, and a gateway killed outright (see verification). History images use the file attachments with which earlier releases passed real PNG checks. Tool-output images as binary results, and tool deferral above 30 tools, are specified by the CLI's schema but were not measured against a vision model. A live session costs about 257 MB of memory, so max: 4 is about 1 GB.
